scenes.headline: RADARS DARK
scenes.caption: May 23, 1967. The three radar sites guarding America from Soviet missiles go dark — all at the same second.
scenes.scene: three BMEWS radar radomes of different designs standing on a warm cream deckle cardstock desk, their phosphor radar sweep lines tearing into coarse 1-bit static as a teletype prints each site name and a red wax date stamp reads 23 MAY 1967
props: radar phosphor screen with a dying green sweep line dissolving into 1-bit static
vintage teletype machine printing the site names CLEAR, THULE, FYLINGDALES
red wax rubber date stamp block reading 23 MAY 1967
scenes.backdrop: warm cream deckle cardstock sheet with faint 1960s blueprint grid

scenes.headline: JAMMING = WAR
scenes.caption: In Cold War doctrine, jamming meant one thing: Soviet attack was imminent. Nuclear-armed bombers were moved to ready-to-launch.
scenes.scene: a typewritten war-doctrine memo card stamped JAMMING = ACT OF WAR in red on a cream cardstock desk beside a B-52 bomber on an alert strip, a punched card reader clattering an ALERT card
scenes.hero: B-52 Stratofortress bomber parked on a runway alert pad, side profile
props: typewritten memo card stamped JAMMING = ACT OF WAR in vermilion red
80-column punched card with ALERT punched across it
1967 Cheyenne Mountain entrance blast door with NORAD sign
scenes.backdrop: warm cream deckle cardstock with a horizontal red ribbon rule

scenes.headline: THE SUN MOVES
scenes.caption: Days earlier, a vast sunspot group had rotated onto the Sun. On May 21 and 23 it erupted — flares, then the century's biggest radio burst.
scenes.scene: a vintage solar observatory sunspot drawing on cream cardstock beside an Olivetti CRT showing a flickering H-alpha flare sequence, a 1-bit frequency axis chart 0.01 to 9.0 GHz spiking in vermilion red, a bulletin card marked IMPORTANCE 3B
scenes.hero: vintage solar observatory drawing of a large irregular sunspot group on the solar disk
props: Olivetti CRT monitor with a 1-bit dithered H-alpha flare sequence on its green screen
1-bit frequency axis chart from 0.01 to 9.0 GHz with a vermilion red burst spike
typewritten solar bulletin card marked IMPORTANCE 3B
scenes.backdrop: cream cardstock with a faint solar graticule circle

scenes.headline: HALF THE SUN
scenes.caption: At Ent Air Force Base, Colorado, forecaster Arnold Snyder got the panicked call. His answer: 'Yes — half the sun has blown away.'
scenes.scene: a 1960s forecaster operations desk with a lifted telephone handset, an oversized typewriter quote card reading HALF THE SUN HAS BLOWN AWAY with a vermilion underline, a teletype printing a 36-48 HOUR STORM FORECAST bulletin

scenes.backdrop: warm cream deckle cardstock with faint punched-paper edge texture

scenes.headline: STAND DOWN
scenes.caption: Forecasters confirmed all three radar sites sat in daylight. As the Sun's burst faded, the 'jamming' faded with it. The launch order never came.
scenes.scene: a vintage 1960s military radio console beside a split signal strip: a descending vermilion solar burst curve on the left mirrored by a radar sweep line returning to green normal on the right, three small radome cards flipped to green checkmarks
scenes.hero: 1960s military radio console with toggle switches, dials and a small CRT

three small radome cards flipped face-up showing green checkmarks
punched alert card stamped VOID in red
scenes.backdrop: cream deckle cardstock with faint signal-grid ruling

scenes.headline: DECLASSIFIED 2016
scenes.caption: The near-war stayed secret for half a century — until 2016, when a declassified study named the culprit: the May 1967 Great Storm.
scenes.scene: a manila folder marked CLASSIFIED receiving a red DECLASSIFIED rubber stamp mid-strike on a cream cardstock desk, beside a typewritten 2016 research paper title card and a punch card feeding through a reader
scenes.hero: manila folder marked CLASSIFIED with a red DECLASSIFIED rubber stamp striking across it
props: typewritten research paper title card reading THE MAY 1967 GREAT STORM

typewriter quote card reading COMMENDABLY RIGHT
scenes.backdrop: cream deckle cardstock with faint redaction-bar texture

scenes.headline: IT WILL HAPPEN AGAIN
scenes.caption: Quebec went dark in 1989. Earth missed a Carrington-class blast by days in 2012. We just passed solar maximum. The Sun never demobilized.
